beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: In ancient Israel, one man stood between the people and God. The high priest carried their gifts and their sins to the altar, and carried God's holiness back to them. It was the most sacred office a person could hold.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: For every high priest taken from among men is ordained for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And here is a tender thing. The high priest was not a distant, perfect being. He was a weak man himself, who knew his own failings, and so he could be gentle with everyone else's. He was one of the people, not above them.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: And no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as was Aaron.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Think of how Aaron became high priest. He did not campaign for it or seize it. God named him, and Moses brought him before the people and set him apart. The honour came down to him; it was never something he grasped.

beats.text: And notice how it was done. Not with a ceremony he arranged for himself, but with another man's hands laid on his head, ordaining him. The authority passed by touch and blessing, from someone who already held it.

beats.text: Then the holy oil was poured over him, running down, and Aaron was consecrated, set apart, given. Everything about that day says the same thing: this was received, not taken.

beats.text: And this is the astonishing part. Even the Lord himself did not make himself a high priest. The Father gave him the office and called him to it. If the Son of God received his authority instead of seizing it, then no one else gets to appoint themselves either.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And that is the quiet good news in this verse. The right to speak and act for God has always come the same way: a real call, and hands laid on a bowed head. It is not earned by being impressive. It is given. So the only question left is a hopeful one. Where might God be calling you?

card.text: No one hands themselves the things of God. Aaron was called, and even Christ was called. That same authority is still given today, by a call and the laying-on of hands. Where is God calling you?
